code.purpose: Monaco editor text; the monospace family also serves compact evidence.

motion.name: motion-fast
motion.purpose: Shared CSS duration for control color, border, and press-state transitions.

motion.name: motion-standard
motion.purpose: Shared CSS/WAAPI duration for bounded arrivals and the measured workspace tab indicator.

motion.name: motion-dialog
motion.purpose: Challenge dialog and backdrop opening; native closing remains immediate.

motion.name: motion-ease
motion.purpose: Shared ease-out for arrivals, tab-indicator movement, dialog opening, and control press movement.

motion.name: control-state
motion.value: background-color var(--motion-fast) ease, color var(--motion-fast) ease, border-color var(--motion-fast) ease, transform var(--motion-fast) var(--motion-ease)
motion.purpose: State transitions for buttons, links, selects, summaries, and textareas. Primary/secondary action buttons translateY(1px) while active; reduced motion suppresses that displacement.

motion.name: workspace-indicator
motion.value: transform var(--motion-standard) var(--motion-ease); transform: translateX(<measured-left>px) scaleX(<measured-width>);
motion.purpose: A one-pixel-wide, two-pixel-high indicator scales and translates to the selected workspace control. First render uses its measured position without a load animation.

motion.name: content-arrival
motion.value: [{ opacity: 0.72 }, { opacity: 1 }]; duration: var(--motion-standard); easing: var(--motion-ease);
motion.purpose: WAAPI arrival on explicit non-code view changes, new notices/retry results, changed replay evidence, and newly opened disclosure content. No initial-page, editor, or keystroke arrival; focus and native disclosure changes remain immediate.

motion.name: followup-arrival
motion.value: [{ opacity: 0.72, transform: translateY(4px) }, { opacity: 1, transform: translateY(0) }]; duration: var(--motion-standard); easing: var(--motion-ease);
motion.purpose: Newly added visible follow-up messages only.

motion.name: dialog-arrival
motion.value: picker-arrive var(--motion-dialog) var(--motion-ease); @keyframes picker-arrive { from { opacity: 0.8; transform: translateY(6px) scale(0.99); } to { opacity: 1; transform: none; } }
motion.purpose: Opening the native challenge picker; closing is not delayed.

motion.name: dialog-backdrop
motion.value: backdrop-arrive var(--motion-dialog) ease-out; @keyframes backdrop-arrive { from { opacity: 0; } to { opacity: 1; } }
motion.purpose: Backdrop opening only; explicitly disabled by reduced motion.

motion.name: recording-pulse
motion.purpose: Live microphone indicators only. The explanation dot pauses while its pane is hidden; reduced motion disables animation.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animation: none !important; transition: none !important; scroll-behavior: auto !important; button:active { transform: none !important; }
motion.purpose: CSS under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. WAAPI checks the preference before starting and cancels active arrivals on a live change; hidden documents/elements are skipped. Follow-up and replay JavaScript scrolling choose auto under reduced motion.

narrative.overview:
SkillRelay is a deliberate practice workspace for coding, explaining technical choices, and reviewing session feedback. The user-approved system uses neutral charcoal throughout, restrained warm amber, and compact controls. It keeps the problem, code, and explanation adjacent on desktop, with the largest flexible area reserved for code. A compact session toolbar leads directly into the work.

This document merges the existing workspace and interaction constraints with the implemented dark system. The visual source of truth is `frontend/src/index.css`, `App.css`, `Learning.css`, the Monaco theme in `components/CodeEditor.jsx`, and shared behavior in `lib/motion.js`, `components/TabIndicator.jsx`, and `components/Disclosure.jsx`. Interface copy must continue to describe real capabilities and saved data accurately; styling does not establish learner outcomes or microphone capture quality.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral dark surfaces separated by tone and thin borders.
Warm amber for the primary action, selection, and keyboard focus.
Compact, left-aligned Manrope text; monospace for code and test values.
Actions beside the work they affect, with evidence available on demand.
A three-column desktop workspace that becomes a naturally scrolling stack.
Brief motion confirms navigation and newly available content without delaying work.

rules.name: The Restrained Accent Rule
rules.body: Use amber for action, selection, and focus; keep ordinary containers and reading surfaces neutral.

rules.name: The Working Type Rule
rules.body: Keep Manrope for interface text and reserve monospace for actual code, examples, and test values.

rules.name: The Tonal Depth Rule
rules.body: Separate working regions with tone and borders; reserve the dialog top layer for an actual modal task.

dos: Do keep the problem, code, and live explanation adjacent on desktop.
Do use neutral surfaces and reserve amber for action, selection, and focus.
Do keep controls beside the work they affect and preserve visible labels.
Do preserve keyboard focus, native disclosure/dialog behavior, and reduced motion.
Do keep real saved summaries, explicit data notices, and useful empty states.
Do retain locally hosted Manrope and use monospace for code and test values.
Do use brief motion to confirm deliberate navigation and newly available content.
donts: Don't restore the large introduction or add a marketing hero to the workspace.
Don't add decorative gradients, glow, generic icon tiles, or repeated colored cards.
Don't shrink supporting text to compensate for excess chrome.
Don't use color alone to communicate selected, failed, or microphone states.
Don't invent streaks, activity, learner outcomes, or saved draft recovery.
Don't imply that visual polish verifies microphone capture, runner isolation, or competition eligibility.
Don't animate initial page load, editor updates, or keystrokes, or delay focus and native closing for motion.
